query: What features can be extracted from a company's business description to predict its regional cluster?

per_column.name: desc_word_count
per_column.rationale: Raw text-length surface feature; generic and unlikely to carry real signal for regional clustering. Values are a sound reading of the source text.

per_column.name: desc_avg_word_length
per_column.rationale: Near-trivial stylometric metric with little analytical leverage for predicting region. Correctly computed from text.

per_column.name: desc_sentence_count
per_column.rationale: Highly skewed (mostly 1), near-constant surface feature; low leverage. Derivable from text.

per_column.name: tech_density
per_column.rationale: A keyword-ratio feature that could plausibly differentiate tech-heavy descriptions; more analytically meaningful than raw length, though the keyword list is opaque. Values are broadly warranted by text.

per_column.name: primary_industry
per_column.rationale: Strong categorical axis for grouping/modeling. But groundedness is shaky: 5AM Ventures (a VC firm) tagged fintech, and Accel (a VC) tagged 'other' while 5AM is fintech—inconsistent; VC labeled fintech is a stretch.

per_column.name: industry_tag_count
per_column.rationale: Could serve as a diversity/breadth feature. But inherits over-tagging errors: 23andme tagged with 3 industries including ai_ml not supported by text; 280 Group tagged education/ai_ml unsupported.

per_column.name: is_fintech
per_column.rationale: Useful binary industry axis. 5AM Ventures (life science VC) flagged fintech is questionable; otherwise reasonable.

per_column.name: is_healthcare
per_column.rationale: Useful axis. 23andme correctly healthcare; but 5AM 'life science' → healthcare AND fintech simultaneously is muddled.

per_column.name: is_enterprise_sw
per_column.rationale: Reasonable axis but near 50/50 and over-applied: Addepar reasonable, but 5AM Ventures (a VC) flagged enterprise_sw is unsupported.

per_column.name: is_consumer
per_column.rationale: Reasonable B2C axis; 23andme consumer is well warranted.

per_column.name: is_security
per_column.rationale: Plausible binary industry flag; sampled rows consistent with text.

per_column.name: is_ai_ml
per_column.rationale: Potentially useful, but clearly over-fired: 23andme and 280 Group both flagged ai_ml with no supporting text mention; 52/199 seems inflated.

per_column.name: is_hardware_iot
per_column.rationale: Reasonable industry flag; sampled rows consistent (all 0).

per_column.name: is_education
per_column.rationale: Plausible flag but 280 Group's 'training, certification' → education is defensible, yet borderline; some over-tagging risk.

per_column.name: mentions_b2b
per_column.rationale: Useful business-model axis; sampled values consistent with text.

per_column.name: mentions_b2c
per_column.rationale: Useful business-model axis; consistent with sampled text.

per_column.name: has_funding_language
per_column.rationale: Reasonable flag; 5AM Ventures 'returns to investors' correctly flagged; others correctly 0.

per_column.name: action_verb_score
per_column.rationale: Generic stylistic/marketing-tone feature with weak connection to regional cluster; values derivable from text.

judge.rationale: The set mixes genuinely useful categorical/industry features (primary_industry, is_* flags, mentions_b2b/b2c, has_funding_language) that offer real axes for grouping and modeling, with several low-leverage surface/stylometric features (word count, avg word length, sentence count, action_verb_score) that add little for this query. Groundedness is generally decent for extractive flags, but the industry tagging over-fires—especially is_ai_ml (fired for 23andme and 280 Group without textual support) and industry_tag_count inheriting these spurious tags—and treatment of VC firms (5AM Ventures, Accel) is inconsistent (life-science VC labeled both fintech and healthcare and enterprise_sw). These represent confident specifics not warranted by the text, lowering the source-groundedness verdict.
